answer: A stake-bonded registry makes each agent identity post a refundable bond before it can trade. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand bonds, so a Sybil attack scales in price instead of being free. Peers only trust identities whose bond sits in an ivory-clear public ledger, and proven fraud slashes the bond and burns the identity like a falcon striking a decoy, at the vertex where cost meets consequence. Honest agents get their bond back; attackers pay for every fake face.
